$comment: THE hand-written part. Four packages -- ui, js, php, py -- are generated from this directory and are never edited. Fix this file, then regenerate. Every fact here is read from Google's own pages, checked 2026-09-15: the discovery document (https://www.googleapis.com/discovery/v1/apis/calendar/v3/rest), the push-notifications guide (https://developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/guides/push) and the events.watch / channels.stop references.
title: Google Calendar

oauth.$refreshTokenRotates: Reusable. Same platform as google-sheets: a refresh response carries access_token, expires_in, scope and token_type and no refresh_token, and Google's own expiry rule is "the refresh token has not been used for six months" -- a statement about a token that is PERSISTED AND REPLAYED.
oauth.$scopeComment: calendar.events is the narrowest scope the events.watch reference lists that also covers events.get and events.list, and channels.stop accepts any Calendar scope. NOT calendar.readonly: a watch is a write to the account's push state. Google's sensitive-scope verification has real lead time -- the host's OAuth app must be verified for this scope before real users can consent.
oauth.$comment: The package DECLARES the dance and does not perform it. A consent screen needs a browser, a redirect URI and somewhere to persist the result, and all three belong to the host. Google's access tokens last ONE HOUR, so a connection that is not refreshed stops working within the day -- which is why refreshToken is required rather than optional.

$sandboxComment: CHECKED 2026-09-15. Google has no test estate for Calendar: there is one API, and a test calendar is a real calendar in somebody's real account. A watch registers a real push channel against it.
sandboxNote: Google has no sandbox for Calendar. A test calendar is a real one in a real account, so every watch and every read is real -- point this at a scratch calendar, not a production one. The faker is the only way to develop against it without touching an account.

credentialFields.label: OAuth client ID
credentialFields.help: From Google Cloud Console -> APIs & Services -> Credentials. ONE value for the whole installation, not per connected account.

credentialFields.label: OAuth client secret
credentialFields.help: The client secret for the same OAuth app. One value for the whole installation.

credentialFields.label: Access token
credentialFields.help: Per connected Google account, and it expires after ONE HOUR. The host refreshes it with the refresh token.

credentialFields.label: Refresh token
credentialFields.help: Per connected Google account. Google issues one only when the consent request asks for offline access; without it the connection dies within the hour.

credentialFields.label: Channel token
credentialFields.help: A secret the host chooses per connected account and sends as `token` on every events.watch. Google echoes it back in the X-Goog-Channel-Token header of every notification, and that echo is the ONLY thing that authenticates a delivery -- Google does not sign them. Up to 256 characters.
